- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80), model frequently overcorrects or overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use lagged 3-day average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model shows persistent bias toward higher prices; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day to reflect low conviction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 0.2–0.5% per day from day 1 to day 30.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral), model tends to drift toward historical mean; use 18-day rolling average as anchor for correction.
